title: Congregational Care
definition: Congregational Care is the shared ministry of watching over, comforting, encouraging, correcting, and helping one another in the body of Christ.
summary: Congregational Care is the shared responsibility of the church body to bear burdens, comfort, encourage, and help one another endure.
christFocus: Jesus Christ cares for His sheep and teaches His people to love one another as He has loved them.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on care that belongs to the whole congregation, not only to leaders. Members visit, pray, provide meals, listen, encourage, admonish, and walk with one another through ordinary and severe trials. It is the daily mercy of the body of Christ in action.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because suffering people often fall through cracks when care is professionalized or assumed to be someone else's job. Congregational care makes love tangible and persistent. It helps the church become a place where burdens are noticed and carried.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask who in your congregation is weary, sick, grieving, recovering, or overwhelmed. Offer specific help rather than vague concern. Build habits of prayer, follow-up, and practical mercy.
